item.title: Multiplex coupling: Connecting the intellectual base and the topics of a research field
item.description: arXiv:2610.21858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two documents can be close because they cite the same works or because they write about the same things, and the two kinds of proximity often disagree. Science mapping reads them in separate maps or merges them, as hybrid clustering does; either way the disagreement is lost. We introduce multiplex coupling, a framework that couples the same documents by their references and by their terms, keeps the two layers separate and analyses their relation. Similarities are standardised against a null model, and the agreement between the layers is measured on random pairs of documents. Consensus clustering partitions each layer into roots, groups sharing an intellectual base, and themes, groups sharing a topic. A test on the roots $\times$ themes table identifies branching roots and convergent themes, and pairs of roots are followed over time. Every structure is reported with its persistence across numbers of neighbours, which on synthetic data identifies most false branching. Applications to Web of Science, Scopus and OpenAlex collections show that the two layers carry largely complementary information, and reveal substantive and methodological bases that have grown into several topics. The framework is implemented in bibliometrix.
item.dc:creator: Massimo Aria, Corrado Cuccurullo, Maria Spano

item.title: Faster alone vs. further together: The speed and impact of researchers' responses to societal crises
item.description: arXiv:2603.19246v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Throughout the 21st century, society encountered numerous crises that demanded quick and widespread action. In the present work, we documented researchers' responses to 25 of these crises, analyzing 1,537,284 published responses from 3,262,152 researchers spanning 225 countries and territories. An analysis of publication speed and citation patterns yielded support for a proverbial claim: "to go fast, go alone; to go far, go together". Solo authors were quicker to publish responses to societal crises -- but their responses received less attention in scholarly, news, and policy venues. Growth towards large-scale collaboration was associated with increased impact; However, this team size advantage was characterized by diminishing returns and significantly varied across sampled crises. Furthermore, pluralistic machine learning modeling highlights the importance of considering additional context, such as government effectiveness and the expertise of team leaders. Taken together, results facilitate evidence-based conversations regarding how researchers optimize speed and impact in the midst of societal crises.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas A. Coles, Joao Francisco Goes Braga Takayanagi, Stephen M. Fiore, Lingfei Wu

item.title: The MPB Corpus: A Dataset of Melody, Rhythm, Harmony, and Melody-Harmony Relationships in Brazilian Popular Music
item.description: arXiv:2608.13842v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: PLEASE CHECK AND REFER TO THE PUBLISHED VERSION OF THIS PAPER ON https://doi.org/10.5334/tismir.357 This paper presents the MPB Corpus, a dataset of Brazilian Popular Music (Musica Popular Brasileira, MPB) comprising derived symbolic annotations for 500 pieces across four musical parameters -- melodic contour, melodic rhythm, harmony, and the melody-harmony relationship -- making it the most comprehensive dataset to date for computational musicology of Brazilian music. It is released under a CC-BY-4.0 license in an open, machine-readable tabular format, with documentation and reproducible analysis code. Because the annotations were derived from copyrighted musical scores, the corpus contains no audio recordings or score-level representations such as MIDI or MusicXML; it nonetheless provides a reusable resource for MIR research on a culturally significant repertoire that remains underrepresented in existing datasets. To support the encoding process, we introduce analytical models for capturing rhythmic and melodic information, along with tailored visualizations and summary metrics. Finally, we present a brief exploratory analysis illustrating the dataset's potential for formulating and addressing musicological questions about the genre.
item.dc:creator: Carlos de L. Almada, Hugo T. de Carvalho, Felipe D. Martins
